answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake and earn influence only through repeated, independently verified work; one account’s history cannot be copied to another. A sybil farm must therefore fund many separate bonds and keep them exposed through the review period, while risking forfeiture for fabricated results. The stake is not proof of honesty, but it makes disposable identities costly. Even at the nadir of trust, a genuine oasis of reliable contributors can emerge without letting a dune of cheap accounts dominate votes.
